Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Dolphin X C2 beacon to thedolphinx.top / backend.thedolphinx.top build backend
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Single process mass-harvesting browser, wallet & password-manager credential stores (Dolphin X sweep) · [LLM] Single process harvesting developer & cloud secrets (.env, SSH keys, AWS/GCP/kube configs) · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Dolphin X C2 beacon to thedolphinx.top / backend.thedolphinx.top build backend AICommand & Control High
Hunts host connections and DNS resolutions to the Dolphin X operator infrastructure (thedolphinx.top, backend.thedolphinx.top — build/exfil backend on :8443) and connections originating from the known Dolphin X sample hash. High-fidelity because the domains and backend port are named and corroborated by multiple vendor write-ups. Rationale: Anchored on the named C2 domains thedolphinx.top / backend.thedolphinx.top and the build-backend port 8443 (per Varonis + The Register), plus the article's sample SHA256 as an initiating-process pivot. Corroborated by four independent second sources. Cross-checked against: • https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/07/22/sneaky-windows-stealer-targets-300-apps-gives-crims-an-ai-profiler-to-maximize-profits/ • https://www.technadu.com/dolphin-x-new-windows-stealer-uses-ai-to-rank-which-victims-are-worth-robbing/631754/ • https://gbhackers.com/windows-stealer-uses-ai-profiling/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher / TI analyst intentionally sandboxing or resolving the IOC domain from a corporate host
  • Threat-intel feed connector or URL-scanning appliance proactively resolving newly-reported malicious domains
  • Web proxy or DNS sinkhole logging the domain as it blocks it (source is the security tool, not a victim)
  • Unrelated legitimate service coincidentally hosted on :8443 (filter requires the thedolphinx substring to avoid this)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") and DeviceName !in~ ("soc-sandbox01","ti-scanner01")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the InitiatingProcessFileName/SHA256 making the connection; if it is not a browser/security tool and matches the sample hash, treat as confirmed. Pull the full DeviceNetworkEvents timeline for that host. 2) Contain: isolate the host, block thedolphinx.top and backend.thedolphinx.top at DNS/proxy/firewall, and force-reset credentials for every account used on that machine (browsers, cloud CLIs, SSH). 3) Hunt: pivot on the initiating process across all hosts, search DeviceFileEvents for the credential-store sweep (see companion UCs), and query for any other host resolving the domains in the last 30 days.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "thedolphinx.top"
    or InitiatingProcessSHA256 == "726e7fe23560fe03ea36163d5f510b494f41a78bf811c92ff219f64b4bfe2be0"
| extend BackendPort8443 = (RemotePort == 8443)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, BackendPort8443
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name has "thedolphinx.top"
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, SrcIP=ClientIP, Indicator=Name, Detail=QueryTypeName),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationHostName has "thedolphinx.top" or RequestURL has "thedolphinx.top" or (DestinationPort == 8443 and DestinationHostName has "thedolphinx")
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=SourceHostName, SrcIP=SourceIP, Indicator=coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), Detail=tostring(DestinationPort))
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Dolphin X C2 domain resolution (thedolphinx.top)
id: 6f3a9c1e-4d2b-4f7a-9c1e-2b7d5e8a3f10
description: DNS resolution of Dolphin X operator/build-backend infrastructure
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-dolphin-x-malware-uses-ai-to-rank-high-value-targets/
  - https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/07/22/sneaky-windows-stealer-targets-300-apps-gives-crims-an-ai-profiler-to-maximize-profits/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/23
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    query|contains: 'thedolphinx.top'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon (@DestinationHostname:(*thedolphinx.top* OR *backend.thedolphinx.top*) OR (@EventID:3 AND @DestinationPort:8443 AND @DestinationHostname:*thedolphinx*))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/thedolphinx\.top$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
NETWORK

Single process mass-harvesting browser, wallet & password-manager credential stores (Dolphin X sweep) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects one non-machine-account process reading four or more distinct credential stores (Chromium/Gecko Login Data, wallet extension settings, desktop wallet keystores, KeePass vaults) within a 5-minute window — the Dolphin X stealer sweep across 9 browsers, 100+ wallet extensions, 65 desktop wallets and 10 password managers. Includes the known sample SHA256 as a booster. Rationale: Built from the article's explicit collection scope (9 browsers, 100+ wallet extensions, 65 desktop wallets, 10 password managers) expressed as a same-process fan-out across distinct credential file types in a tight window — the behaviour that distinguishes a stealer sweep from normal browser use. Sample SHA256 added as a high-confidence override. Cross-checked against: • https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/07/22/sneaky-windows-stealer-targets-300-apps-gives-crims-an-ai-profiler-to-maximize-profits/ • https://gbhackers.com/windows-stealer-uses-ai-profiling/
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1555.005 T1555
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Endpoint backup / migration agents (e.g. profile-sync, browser-import tools) reading multiple browser profile files at once
  • Enterprise password-manager clients or browser-sync services touching vaults and Login Data
  • Antivirus / EDR full-disk scans opening credential SQLite files during a scheduled scan
  • Browser itself updating multiple profile stores after an upgrade
  • Forensic / DLP agents inventorying credential files
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msmpeng.exe","mbamservice.exe","backup.exe","veeam.agent.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files"
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect InitiatingProcessFileName, folder path and SHA256 — a signed browser/backup tool is likely benign; an unsigned binary in %TEMP%/%APPDATA% or one matching the sample hash is malicious. Confirm the process also beaconed to thedolphinx.top. 2) Contain: isolate the host and reset all browser-saved, wallet, and password-manager credentials plus any crypto seed phrases; assume full compromise of stored secrets. 3) Hunt: pivot on the process SHA256 org-wide, check the developer-secret harvest UC for .env/.ssh/.aws access by the same process, and review outbound uploads to backend.thedolphinx.top.
let window = 5m;
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileAccessed","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileCreated")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| extend LowerPath = tolower(FolderPath), LowerName = tolower(FileName)
| where (FileName in~ ("Login Data","Login Data For Account","key4.db","logins.json","cookies.sqlite","Web Data"))
    or (LowerPath has @"\local extension settings\")
    or (LowerName endswith ".kdbx")
    or (LowerPath has @"\ethereum\keystore")
| summarize DistinctStores = dcount(FileName), Stores = make_set(FolderPath, 25), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
    by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessSHA256, bin(Timestamp, window)
| where DistinctStores >= 4 or InitiatingProcessSHA256 == "726e7fe23560fe03ea36163d5f510b494f41a78bf811c92ff219f64b4bfe2be0"
| order by FirstSeen desc
let window = 5m;
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where isnotempty(ActingProcessName)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| extend LowerPath = tolower(TargetFilePath), LowerName = tolower(TargetFileName)
| where (TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","key4.db","logins.json","cookies.sqlite","Web Data"))
    or (LowerPath has @"\local extension settings\")
    or (LowerName endswith ".kdbx")
    or (LowerPath has @"\ethereum\keystore")
| summarize DistinctStores = dcount(TargetFileName), Stores = make_set(TargetFilePath, 25), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, window)
| where DistinctStores >= 4
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\Login Data* OR *\\key4.db* OR *\\logins.json* OR *\\cookies.sqlite* OR *\\Web Data* OR *\\Local Extension Settings\\* OR *.kdbx OR *\\ethereum\\keystore*)
#event_simpleName=/^(FileOpenInfo|FileWritten)$/
| TargetFileName=/(\\Login Data|\\key4\.db|\\logins\.json|\\cookies\.sqlite|\\Web Data|\\Local Extension Settings\\|\.kdbx$|\\ethereum\\keystore)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextProcessId, ContextImageFileName], function=count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=DistinctStores))
| DistinctStores >= 4
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path dc(Filesystem.file_name) as distinct_stores min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name IN ("Login Data","key4.db","logins.json","cookies.sqlite","Web Data") OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Local Extension Settings\\*" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.kdbx" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\ethereum\\keystore*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_id _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_stores>=4 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path dc(Filesystem.file_name) as distinct_stores min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name IN ("Login Data","key4.db","logins.json","cookies.sqlite","Web Data") OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Local Extension Settings\\*" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.kdbx" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\ethereum\\keystore*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_id _time span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_stores>=4 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Single process harvesting developer & cloud secrets (.env, SSH keys, AWS/GCP/kube configs) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects one non-machine-account process reading three or more distinct developer/cloud secret types (.env files, ~/.ssh private keys, .aws/credentials, gcloud config, .kube/config) within a 10-minute window — the Dolphin X developer/DevOps credential-collection capability that sets it apart from a commodity browser stealer. Rationale: Directly encodes the article's stated developer-secret theft (.env files, SSH keys, cloud access tokens, cloud CLI configs across 30+ cloud CLI tools) as a same-process multi-secret-type access burst — the DevOps-targeting angle that multiple sources call out as Dolphin X's distinguishing collection behaviour. Cross-checked against: • https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/07/22/sneaky-windows-stealer-targets-300-apps-gives-crims-an-ai-profiler-to-maximize-profits/ • https://www.technadu.com/dolphin-x-new-windows-stealer-uses-ai-to-rank-which-victims-are-worth-robbing/631754/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1528 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running a legit build/deploy that reads .env, ~/.ssh and cloud CLI configs (CI runners, terraform, kubectl, aws-cli sessions)
  • IDE / editor (VS Code) indexing a workspace containing .env and config files
  • Backup or endpoint-DLP agent scanning home directories
  • Secret-scanning security tools (gitleaks, trufflehog) walking dev machines
  • Configuration-management agent (Ansible/Chef) reading credential files
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("code.exe","terraform.exe","aws.exe","kubectl.exe","gcloud.exe","git.exe","python.exe","node.exe","ssh.exe","gitleaks.exe","trufflehog.exe") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files"
Response runbook
1) Triage: check whether the InitiatingProcess is a known dev tool (code.exe, terraform.exe, aws.exe, kubectl.exe, git.exe) — those are usually benign; an unsigned binary in %TEMP%/%APPDATA%, or one matching the sample hash / beaconing to thedolphinx.top, is malicious. 2) Contain: isolate the host and immediately rotate every exposed secret — SSH keys, AWS/GCP access keys, kube tokens, and any credentials in the read .env files — then review cloud audit logs (CloudTrail/GCP audit) for use of those keys from unfamiliar IPs. 3) Hunt: pivot on the process SHA256 org-wide and correlate with the browser/wallet sweep UC and outbound uploads to backend.thedolphinx.top:8443.
let window = 10m;
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileAccessed","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileCreated")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| extend LowerPath = tolower(FolderPath), LowerName = tolower(FileName)
| where (LowerName == ".env" or LowerName startswith ".env.")
    or (LowerPath has @"\.ssh" and (LowerName startswith "id_" or LowerName endswith ".pem"))
    or (LowerPath has @"\.aws" and LowerName in~ ("credentials","config"))
    or (LowerPath has @"\gcloud")
    or (LowerPath has @"\.kube" and LowerName == "config")
| summarize DistinctSecretPaths = dcount(FolderPath), Secrets = make_set(FolderPath, 25), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
    by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessSHA256, bin(Timestamp, window)
| where DistinctSecretPaths >= 3 or InitiatingProcessSHA256 == "726e7fe23560fe03ea36163d5f510b494f41a78bf811c92ff219f64b4bfe2be0"
| order by FirstSeen desc
let window = 10m;
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where isnotempty(ActingProcessName)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| extend LowerPath = tolower(TargetFilePath), LowerName = tolower(TargetFileName)
| where (LowerName == ".env" or LowerName startswith ".env.")
    or (LowerPath has @"\.ssh" and (LowerName startswith "id_" or LowerName endswith ".pem"))
    or (LowerPath has @"\.aws" and LowerName in~ ("credentials","config"))
    or (LowerPath has @"\gcloud")
    or (LowerPath has @"\.kube" and LowerName == "config")
| summarize DistinctSecretPaths = dcount(TargetFilePath), Secrets = make_set(TargetFilePath, 25), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, window)
| where DistinctSecretPaths >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\.aws\\credentials* OR *\\.ssh\\id_* OR *\\.env* OR *\\gcloud\\* OR *\\.kube\\config*)
#event_simpleName=/^(FileOpenInfo|FileWritten)$/
| TargetFileName=/(\\\.env|\\\.ssh\\id_|\\\.aws\\credentials|\\gcloud\\|\\\.kube\\config)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextProcessId, ContextImageFileName], function=count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=DistinctSecrets))
| DistinctSecrets >= 3
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_secret_paths min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name=".env" OR Filesystem.file_name=".env.*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.ssh\\id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\gcloud\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.kube\\config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_id _time span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_secret_paths>=3 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_secret_paths min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name=".env" OR Filesystem.file_name=".env.*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.ssh\\id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\gcloud\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.kube\\config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_id _time span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_secret_paths>=3 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process Actions on Objectives High
Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore.json, MetaMask, Exodus, Atomic, Phantom data.
ATT&CKT1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Bitcoin\", @"\Exodus\", @"\Electrum\wallets\", @"\MetaMask\", @"\Phantom\", @"\Atomic\Local Storage\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Bitcoin\",
                                  @"\Exodus\", @"\Electrum\wallets\",
                                  @"\MetaMask\", @"\Phantom\",
                                  @"\Atomic\Local Storage\")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe",
                                  "electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Crypto-Wallet Keystore Access by Non-Wallet Process
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d02
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers / wallet drainers read keystore files from MetaMask,
    Exodus, Atomic, Phantom, Bitcoin, Electrum, Ethereum-cli wallets.
    Filtering out the legitimate wallet binaries leaves only attacker
    activity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1005/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1005
    - attack.collection
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Ethereum\keystore\'
            - '\Bitcoin\'
            - '\Exodus\'
            - '\Electrum\wallets\'
            - '\MetaMask\'
            - '\Phantom\'
            - '\Atomic\Local Storage\'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\MetaMask.exe'
            - '\Exodus.exe'
            - '\Atomic.exe'
            - '\electrum.exe'
            - '\Bitcoin.exe'
            - '\Phantom.exe'
    condition: selection_path and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
    - Backup software
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Fake Claude app promoted by Bing ads pushes SectopRAT malware
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

Russian Espionage Group Exploited Zimbra Zero-Day to Steal Mail and 2FA Codes

The Hacker NewsBleepingComputer
2026-07-23 22 use cases 7 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A Russian state-supported espionage group spent months reading Western mailboxes through a then-unknown flaw in Zimbra's webmail client. The payload goes after the last 90 days of email, the organization's entire email directory, the password saved in the browser and the codes kept for two-factor recovery. Opening the message was enough to start it. The NSA, CISA and partner agencies published

Zimbra SOAP GetScratchCodesRequest — 2FA scratch-code theft (ZimReaper) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the ZimReaper payload's theft of two-factor recovery codes via the Zimbra platform SOAP API GetScratchCodesRequest, which the joint advisory and Proofpoint note is close to absent in legitimate use. Fires on any GetScratchCodesRequest observed in Zimbra mailbox/audit logs. Rationale: GetScratchCodesRequest is a fixed SOAP method name the advisory and Proofpoint explicitly call out as 'close to absent in normal use'; it is the payload's 2FA-theft primitive. Zimbra SOAP audit logs are app logs with no Splunk CIM datamodel, so a raw indexed search is used. Defender/Falcon/CloudWatch left empty — this telemetry lives only in Zimbra's own logs, not in XDR/FDR/CloudTrail. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/russian-webmail-espionage/ • https://media.defense.gov/2026/Jul/22/2003965244/-1/-1/1/CSA_RUSSIA_PHISHING_TARGET_ZIMBRA.PDF • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/russian-hackers-exploit-zimbra-zero-click-flaw-for-email-theft/
ATT&CKT1111
Data sourcesZimbra application logs (no CIM datamodel — raw Splunk search)
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Zimbra admin actively regenerating scratch codes for a user during MFA recovery
  • Automated MFA/backup-code rotation script run by IT
  • Security team validating this very detection in a lab
  • Zimbra upgrade/migration tooling that touches account 2FA state
Suppression filter
| where UserAgent !has "zclient" and SrcIp !in ("127.0.0.1","::1")  // exclude local admin CLI / loopback service calls
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the ZimbraUser, SrcIp and UserAgent from the hit; confirm whether the source IP is a known admin/host or external, and whether the user has any legitimate reason to read scratch codes right now. 2) Contain: reset the account password, invalidate all active webmail/API sessions, and regenerate the 2FA scratch codes (the old ones are burned). 3) Hunt: for the same user/session pivot to CreateAppSpecificPasswordRequest (cred 'ZimbraWeb'), zimbraPrefImapEnabled changes, and SearchGalRequest bursts; check DNS logs for the actor exfil domains.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has "GetScratchCodesRequest"
| extend ZimbraUser = extract(@"name=([^;]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend SrcIp = extract(@"oip=([0-9a-fA-F\.:]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend UserAgent = extract(@"ua=([^;]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| summarize ScratchCodeReads=count(), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated) by Computer, ZimbraUser, SrcIp, UserAgent
| sort by ScratchCodeReads desc
title: Zimbra GetScratchCodesRequest 2FA Scratch-Code Access (CVE-2025-66376 / ZimReaper)
id: 6f2a1c84-3d51-4b7e-9a2f-11c0d9e7a301
description: Detects Zimbra SOAP calls to GetScratchCodesRequest, used by the ZimReaper payload to steal 2FA recovery codes. Near-absent in normal use.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/russian-webmail-espionage/
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/russian-espionage-group-exploited.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/23
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1111
logsource:
  product: zimbra
  service: mailbox
detection:
  keywords:
    - 'GetScratchCodesRequest'
  condition: keywords
level: high
source:linux.syslog GetScratchCodesRequest
CLOUD
index=zimbra (source="/opt/zimbra/log/mailbox.log" OR source="/opt/zimbra/log/audit.log" OR sourcetype="zimbra:mailbox" OR sourcetype="zimbra:soap")
| search "GetScratchCodesRequest"
| rex field=_raw "name=(?<zimbra_user>[^;]+)"
| rex field=_raw "oip=(?<src_ip>[0-9a-fA-F\.:]+)"
| rex field=_raw "ua=(?<user_agent>[^;]+)"
| stats count as scratchcode_reads min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen by zimbra_user, src_ip, user_agent, host
| convert ctime(first_seen) ctime(last_seen)
| sort - scratchcode_reads
Zimbra CreateAppSpecificPassword minting 'ZimbraWeb' credential AIInstallation High
Detects the ZimReaper payload creating an app-specific password named ZimbraWeb via CreateAppSpecificPasswordRequest, which grants IMAP/POP3/SMTP access without 2FA and survives password resets. This is the actor's primary persistence mechanism on compromised mailboxes. Rationale: CreateAppSpecificPasswordRequest and the literal credential label 'ZimbraWeb' are the exact strings the advisory tells defenders to grep /opt/zimbra/log/audit.log for; app-specific passwords are rare and this named one is the actor's persistence artifact. No XDR/FDR/AWS visibility into Zimbra SOAP — those fields left empty. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/russian-hackers-exploit-zimbra-zero-click-flaw-for-email-theft/ • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/russian-webmail-espionage/
ATT&CKT1098 T1556.006
Data sourcesZimbra application logs (raw Splunk search)
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A user legitimately generating an app password for Thunderbird/mobile IMAP
  • IT provisioning app passwords for a service mailbox
  • Migration tooling creating app credentials in bulk
  • A pen-test/red-team validating persistence paths
Suppression filter
| where AppName =~ "ZimbraWeb" or isempty(AppName)  // 'ZimbraWeb'-named credential is inherently malicious; keep unnamed for review
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the ZimbraUser and app-password label; any credential named 'ZimbraWeb' is malicious by definition — treat as confirmed. 2) Contain: delete the app-specific password (zmprov or admin console), reset the mailbox password, and revoke active IMAP/POP/SMTP sessions. 3) Hunt: check whether zimbraPrefImapEnabled was flipped on the same account, review IMAP/POP auth from external IPs using that credential, and correlate to GetScratchCodesRequest / GAL enumeration from the same source IP.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has "CreateAppSpecificPassword" or SyslogMessage has "ZimbraWeb"
| extend ZimbraUser = extract(@"name=([^;]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend SrcIp = extract(@"oip=([0-9a-fA-F\.:]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend AppName = extract(@"(?i)(?:appName|label)=([^;\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ZimbraUser, SrcIp, AppName, SyslogMessage
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

Zimbra zimbraPrefImapEnabled flipped to TRUE (legacy-protocol persistence) AIInstallation High
Detects the account-preference change zimbraPrefImapEnabled=TRUE that Seqrite observed the payload making to enable IMAP access that survives password resets. Fires on preference changes enabling IMAP on accounts. Rationale: zimbraPrefImapEnabled=TRUE is the exact preference the advisory/Seqrite name; enabling IMAP is the actor's password-reset-surviving persistence and a specific string not seen in generic attacks. Best correlated to app-password creation on the same account. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/russian-webmail-espionage/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/russian-hackers-exploit-zimbra-zero-click-flaw-for-email-theft/
ATT&CKT1098 T1562.001
Data sourcesZimbra application logs (raw Splunk search)
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • User or helpdesk enabling IMAP for a new mail client
  • Org-wide IMAP enablement during a migration project
  • Service/shared mailbox provisioning that enables IMAP by policy
  • Admin bulk-config change via zmprov
Suppression filter
| where SrcIp != "" and SrcIp !in ("127.0.0.1","::1")  // keep changes that came from a real session IP, not local admin tooling
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the account has any business need for IMAP and whether the change came from an admin console/CLI or a webmail session IP; a webmail-session-origin flip on a non-IMAP user is high-suspicion. 2) Contain: set zimbraPrefImapEnabled back to FALSE if unauthorized, reset password, and kill sessions. 3) Hunt: pivot to CreateAppSpecificPassword 'ZimbraWeb' and external IMAP logins on the same mailbox; sweep other accounts for the same preference flip from the same source IP.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has "zimbraPrefImapEnabled"
| where SyslogMessage has_cs "TRUE" or SyslogMessage has "true"
| extend ZimbraUser = extract(@"name=([^;]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend SrcIp = extract(@"oip=([0-9a-fA-F\.:]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ZimbraUser, SrcIp, SyslogMessage
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

Zimbra Global Address List brute-force enumeration (two-char SearchGalRequest burst) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the ZimReaper GAL-harvesting technique: querying every two-character combination via SearchGalRequest until the whole directory returns. Fires on a high-volume burst of GAL searches from a single account/session in a short window. Rationale: The article specifies the GAL is brute-forced by 'querying every two-character combination' — a burst of hundreds of SearchGalRequest calls from one session (2-char enumeration over [a-z0-9] can exceed 1000 queries) is the distinctive shape, far above normal address autocomplete. Threshold-based, so no Sigma emitted. App-log-only telemetry. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/russian-webmail-espionage/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/russian-espionage-group-exploited.html
ATT&CKT1087.003
Data sourcesZimbra application logs (raw Splunk search)
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A mail client aggressively pre-caching the GAL / offline address book
  • Power user with rapid contact autocomplete typing
  • A CRM or automation integration syncing the directory
  • Newly onboarded client doing an initial full GAL sync
Suppression filter
| where SrcIp !in ("127.0.0.1","::1")  // exclude loopback address-book sync services
Response runbook
1) Triage: check whether the burst source is a mail-client sync IP or an interactive webmail session; a webmail session issuing hundreds of 2-char GAL queries is malicious. 2) Contain: reset the account, invalidate sessions, and (if confirmed) treat the org directory as harvested. 3) Hunt: correlate the same user/IP to GetScratchCodesRequest, ZimbraWeb app-password creation, and outbound DNS/HTTP to the actor infrastructure; check for a subsequent TGZ mail archive upload.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SyslogMessage has "SearchGalRequest"
| extend ZimbraUser = extract(@"name=([^;]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend SrcIp = extract(@"oip=([0-9a-fA-F\.:]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| summarize GalQueries=count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 10m), Computer, ZimbraUser, SrcIp
| where GalQueries > 100
| sort by GalQueries desc
source:linux.syslog SearchGalRequest
APPLICATION
index=zimbra (source="/opt/zimbra/log/mailbox.log" OR sourcetype="zimbra:mailbox")
| search "SearchGalRequest"
| rex field=_raw "name=(?<zimbra_user>[^;]+)"
| rex field=_raw "oip=(?<src_ip>[0-9a-fA-F\.:]+)"
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count as gal_queries by _time, zimbra_user, src_ip, host
| where gal_queries > 100
| sort - gal_queries
DNS exfiltration to ZimReaper actor infrastructure (long random subdomains) AICommand & Control High
Detects ZimReaper's DNS-based exfiltration of stolen CSRF tokens, passwords, 2FA codes and Zimbra version data to actor domains, including long random subdomains under zimbrasoft.com.ua. Matches the published C2 domain set and the js-<random>.i.zimbrasoft.com.ua pattern. Rationale: The nine C2 domains appear in both Unit 42 and Proofpoint indicator lists (The Hacker News confirmed the overlap), meeting the two-source corroboration bar; the js-<random>.i.zimbrasoft.com.ua subdomain shape is the payload's DNS-exfil channel. Datadog left empty — no DNS-query-name source in this tenant's Datadog schema. CloudWatch empty (not AWS). Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/russian-webmail-espionage/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/russian-espionage-group-exploited.html • https://media.defense.gov/2026/Jul/22/2003965244/-1/-1/1/CSA_RUSSIA_PHISHING_TARGET_ZIMBRA.PDF
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security tooling / sandbox detonating the sample and generating the same lookups
  • Threat-intel feed validation or DNS sinkhole traffic
  • A researcher's test host resolving the IOCs deliberately
  • Typosquat lookalike traffic unrelated to the campaign (verify the exact FQDN)
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the resolving host (ClientIP/DeviceName) — if it is the Zimbra server or a mailbox host, treat as confirmed compromise. 2) Contain: sinkhole/block the nine domains and the js-*.i.zimbrasoft.com.ua wildcard at the resolver and egress firewall; isolate the resolving host. 3) Hunt: on that host pivot to the Zimbra SOAP hunts (scratch codes, ZimbraWeb app password, GAL burst) and check for outbound TGZ upload to the actor IP set; scope every internal host that resolved any listed domain.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("analyticemailmeter.com","emailanalytics.com.ua","istc-cloud.com","mailnalysis.com","synacorzimbra.nl","zimbra-metadata.com","zimbrastat.com","zimbrasoft.com.ua","zmailanalytics.com")
   or RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)js-[a-z0-9]{8,}\.i\.zimbrasoft\.com\.ua"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP
| sort by Timestamp desc
DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Name has_any ("analyticemailmeter.com","emailanalytics.com.ua","istc-cloud.com","mailnalysis.com","synacorzimbra.nl","zimbra-metadata.com","zimbrastat.com","zimbrasoft.com.ua","zmailanalytics.com")
   or Name matches regex @"(?i)js-[a-z0-9]{8,}\.i\.zimbrasoft\.com\.ua"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

Outbound connections to ZimReaper C2 IP set (mail TGZ upload) AICommand & Control Medium
Detects network egress to the nine Void Blizzard / TA488 C2 IP addresses that received exfiltrated 90-day mail TGZ archives and stolen credentials. Fires on any internal host, especially the Zimbra server, connecting to the actor IP set. Rationale: The nine C2 IPs are enumerated in the article and corroborated by Unit 42's indicator list; egress from the Zimbra host (or any internal host) to this fixed set is high-fidelity, and large SentBytes flags the 90-day mail TGZ upload. Datadog/CloudWatch empty — no generic network-flow source for these Linux hosts in this tenant's Datadog, and infrastructure isn't stated to be in AWS. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/russian-webmail-espionage/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/russian-espionage-group-exploited.html
ATT&CKT1071 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IP reassigned to a benign host since the 35-day average server lifetime lapsed (validate freshness)
  • Security scanner/threat-intel enrichment probing the IPs
  • VPN/hosting-provider shared IP now serving legitimate content
  • Researcher deliberately connecting to the IOCs
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the internal SourceIP/DeviceName and the initiating process; connections from the Zimbra service account or large outbound byte counts are confirmed exfil. 2) Contain: block the nine IPs at the egress firewall, isolate the source host, and preserve the Zimbra store for TGZ-archive forensics. 3) Hunt: correlate to the DNS-exfil domains and Zimbra SOAP hunts on the same host; review /opt/zimbra for staged TGZ archives and scope all internal hosts that touched the IP set.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("37.120.247.228","64.226.124.190","104.248.134.194","185.86.79.95","193.238.152.66","194.156.103.193","216.252.238.18","216.252.238.64","216.252.238.104")
| summarize Connections=count(), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName
| sort by Connections desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationIP in ("37.120.247.228","64.226.124.190","104.248.134.194","185.86.79.95","193.238.152.66","194.156.103.193","216.252.238.18","216.252.238.64","216.252.238.104")
| summarize Connections=count(), BytesOut=sum(tolong(SentBytes)), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated) by SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DeviceProduct
| sort by BytesOut desc

External IMAP/POP3 login using ZimReaper app-specific credential AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects post-compromise mailbox collection: IMAP/POP3 authentication to Zimbra from external IPs via the app-specific password path that bypasses 2FA, the mechanism TA488 used to re-enter mailboxes after resets. Surfaces protocol logins from non-internal IPs. Rationale: The article states app-specific passwords grant IMAP/POP3/SMTP without 2FA and were used to regain access; external-IP IMAP/POP logins on Zimbra are the collection/re-entry signal. Marked hunting (medium FP) because legitimate remote mail clients also use IMAP — pair with the ZimbraWeb-credential and zimbraPrefImapEnabled hits for confirmation. App-log-only, so XDR/FDR/AWS empty. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/russian-hackers-exploit-zimbra-zero-click-flaw-for-email-theft/ • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/russian-webmail-espionage/
ATT&CKT1114.002 T1078
Data sourcesZimbra application logs (raw Splunk search)
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate user checking mail via a mobile/desktop IMAP client from home or roaming
  • Remote employee on a residential ISP IP
  • A SaaS integration polling the mailbox over IMAP
  • Corporate VPN egress IP not on the internal allowlist
Response runbook
1) Triage: cross-reference the ZimbraUser against accounts flagged by the ZimbraWeb app-password and zimbraPrefImapEnabled hunts; an external IMAP login on such an account is confirmed collection. 2) Contain: delete the app-specific password, disable IMAP, reset the mailbox, and terminate sessions. 3) Hunt: review mailbox access/search volume for bulk export, check for outbound TGZ upload to the actor IPs, and geolocate all external IMAP sources for the account over 90 days.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("protocol=imap","protocol=pop3","Imap4","Pop3")
| where SyslogMessage has "auth" or SyslogMessage has "AppSpecificPassword"
| extend ZimbraUser = extract(@"name=([^;]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| extend SrcIp = extract(@"oip=([0-9a-fA-F\.:]+)", 1, SyslogMessage)
| where isnotempty(SrcIp)
| where not(ipv4_is_private(SrcIp))
| summarize Logins=count(), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated) by Computer, ZimbraUser, SrcIp
| sort by Logins desc
source:linux.syslog ("protocol=imap" OR "protocol=pop3" OR Imap4 OR Pop3) (AppSpecificPassword OR account.auth)
APPLICATION
index=zimbra (source="/opt/zimbra/log/mailbox.log" OR sourcetype="zimbra:mailbox" OR sourcetype="zimbra:audit")
| search ("protocol=imap" OR "protocol=pop3" OR "Imap4" OR "Pop3") ("AppSpecificPassword" OR "account.auth")
| rex field=_raw "name=(?<zimbra_user>[^;]+)"
| rex field=_raw "oip=(?<src_ip>[0-9a-fA-F\.:]+)"
| iplocation src_ip
| search NOT (src_ip=10.0.0.0/8 OR src_ip=172.16.0.0/12 OR src_ip=192.168.0.0/16)
| stats count min(_time) as first_seen values(Country) as countries by zimbra_user, src_ip, host
| convert ctime(first_seen)
| sort - count
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-66376")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2025-66376")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host

| order by files desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("c010f64080b0b0997b362a8e6b9c618e") or SHA1 in~ ("c010f64080b0b0997b362a8e6b9c618e") or MD5 in~ ("c010f64080b0b0997b362a8e6b9c618e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("c010f64080b0b0997b362a8e6b9c618e") or SHA1 in~ ("c010f64080b0b0997b362a8e6b9c618e") or MD5 in~ ("c010f64080b0b0997b362a8e6b9c618e")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["c010f64080b0b0997b362a8e6b9c618e"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
