Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] msaRAT delivery: curl downloads update_ms.msi to ProgramData over plain-HTTP 443
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Don’t swing at everything
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] msaRAT install: msiexec executing ProgramData MSI masquerading as Windows update · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] msaRAT C2: Chrome/Edge launched with --remote-debugging-port for CDP hijack · [LLM] msaRAT defense evasion: browser plain-HTTP over 443 to known msaRAT infrastructure · [LLM] msaRAT WebRTC: debug-launched browser initiating STUN/relay signaling · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
msaRAT delivery: curl downloads update_ms.msi to ProgramData over plain-HTTP 443 AIDelivery Medium
Hunts msaRAT's initial delivery: a curl (or wget) invocation that pulls an MSI payload into C:\ProgramData, as flagged by Talos. Article-specific because it pins the LOLBin (curl), the file type (.msi) and the staging directory (ProgramData) together in one command line. Rationale: Uses Talos's explicit guidance ('unusual curl commands downloading MSI files to the ProgramData directory') — the curl+.msi+ProgramData triple is far more specific than any single token and rarely co-occurs in benign admin activity.
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate software vendors packaging MSI installers staged in ProgramData by a management agent
  • IT scripts that pre-download MSI packages via curl for offline install
  • Chocolatey/winget helper flows that fetch MSI to a ProgramData cache
  • Security tooling self-updaters that pull MSI over curl
  • RMM agents staging patches in ProgramData
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("choco.exe","winget.exe","msiexec.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full curl command line and the source URL/IP; check whether the destination resolves to 172.86.126.18 or a *.workers.dev host, and whether the MSI name mimics a Windows update. 2) Contain: isolate the host, quarantine the downloaded MSI, and block the source URL/IP at the proxy/firewall. 3) Hunt: look on the same host for msiexec executing that MSI, and for chrome.exe/msedge.exe subsequently launched with --remote-debugging-port (CDP hijack).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("curl.exe","wget.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has ".msi" and ProcessCommandLine has "ProgramData"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\curl.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\wget.exe"
| where CommandLine has ".msi" and CommandLine has "ProgramData"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

msaRAT install: msiexec executing ProgramData MSI masquerading as Windows update AIInstallation Medium
Hunts execution of the msaRAT MSI from ProgramData where the invocation impersonates a Windows update/patch. Article-specific: Talos states the infection starts with 'a deceptive MSI file masquerading as a Windows update' that loads the payload into memory. Rationale: Anchors on Talos's 'MSI masquerading as a Windows update' plus the ProgramData staging path; the lure keywords (update/patch/windows/kb) inside an msiexec command line pointed at ProgramData is the specific masquerade the article describes.
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1036.005 T1218.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • WSUS/SCCM/Intune deploying genuine update MSIs from a ProgramData cache
  • Third-party patch-management tools (Ivanti, PDQ) staging MSIs in ProgramData
  • Vendor updaters naming their MSI with 'update' in the filename
  • Driver/firmware update utilities using msiexec from ProgramData
  • Windows feature-on-demand helper packages
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ccmexec.exe","tiworker.exe","pdq.exe","pdqdeployrunner.exe","ivanti.patch.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the MSI's provenance — is it signed, and does the parent process match a known patch-management agent? Check the file hash against the Talos IOC set. 2) Contain: if unsigned or curl-delivered, isolate the host and quarantine the MSI before it maps the payload into memory. 3) Hunt: pivot to browser processes on the host for --remote-debugging-port launches and outbound traffic to 172.86.126.18 / is-01-ast.ols-img-12.workers.dev.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "msiexec.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "ProgramData" and ProcessCommandLine has ".msi"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("update","patch","windows","kb")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\msiexec.exe"
| where CommandLine has "ProgramData" and CommandLine has ".msi"
| where CommandLine has_any ("update","patch","windows","kb")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

msaRAT C2: Chrome/Edge launched with --remote-debugging-port for CDP hijack AICommand & Control High
Hunts the msaRAT C2 primitive: an unexpected parent spawning chrome.exe/msedge.exe with a --remote-debugging-port flag to open a Chrome DevTools Protocol channel. Article-specific: Talos describes C2 established by 'hijacking Chrome or Edge browsers via the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP).' Rationale: The --remote-debugging-port flag is the concrete on-host artefact of CDP abuse Talos names; excluding developer/IDE parents keeps the true-positive signal (a non-browser, non-dev parent opening a debug port) while cutting the main benign source.
ATT&CKT1205 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developers running Selenium/Puppeteer/Playwright automation that launches a browser with a debug port
  • QA/CI runners using chromedriver/msedgedriver harnesses
  • Electron apps spawning a Chromium child with debugging enabled
  • Browser extension developers testing with remote debugging
  • Automated screenshot/scraping services on the endpoint
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("node.exe","python.exe","pwsh.exe","selenium.exe","chromedriver.exe","msedgedriver.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the parent process — a browser debug port opened by curl, msiexec, or an unknown binary (not an IDE/automation framework) is high-signal. Capture the port number. 2) Contain: kill the browser and parent process, isolate the host, and inspect for loopback traffic to the debug port from a non-browser process. 3) Hunt: correlate with outbound connections to 172.86.126.18 / *.workers.dev and with prior ProgramData MSI execution on the same host.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--remote-debugging-port"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("explorer.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","devenv.exe","code.exe","chromedriver.exe","msedgedriver.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\chrome.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\msedge.exe"
| where CommandLine has "--remote-debugging-port"
| where not(ParentProcessName endswith "\\explorer.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\chrome.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\msedge.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\devenv.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\code.exe")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

msaRAT defense evasion: browser plain-HTTP over 443 to known msaRAT infrastructure AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts msaRAT's network-evasion behaviour — routing C2 through a legitimate browser process to the campaign's confirmed infrastructure (172.86.126.18 / is-01-ast.ols-img-12.workers.dev), including plaintext HTTP on port 443. Article-specific: Talos warns to 'watch for sending plain HTTP traffic over port 443' via legitimate browser processes. Rationale: Pins Talos's confirmed C2 IP (172.86.126.18) and workers.dev host with a browser initiating-process and port 443, matching the article's 'plain HTTP over 443 via legitimate browser' evasion description — an exact-IOC match is inherently high fidelity.
ATT&CKT1572 T1090.001 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Benign browsing that happens to resolve to a reused Cloudflare Workers IP (shared infra)
  • Corporate proxy re-writing SNI so ApplicationProtocol is mislabeled
  • Security scanners probing the flagged IP for validation
  • Threat-intel enrichment tooling connecting to the IOC deliberately
  • Sinkhole/DNS-RPZ redirect traffic hitting the same host
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the browser process on the host was recently launched with --remote-debugging-port and whether the connection carried cleartext HTTP on 443. 2) Contain: block 172.86.126.18 and is-01-ast.ols-img-12.workers.dev at egress, isolate the host, and preserve the browser process for memory analysis. 3) Hunt: sweep the org for any other host contacting these IOCs and for ProgramData MSI + msiexec masquerade activity preceding the connection.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe")
| where RemoteIP == "172.86.126.18" or RemoteUrl endswith "is-01-ast.ols-img-12.workers.dev"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationIP == "172.86.126.18" or DestinationHostName endswith "is-01-ast.ols-img-12.workers.dev"
| where DestinationPort == 443
| where ApplicationProtocol =~ "http" or isempty(ApplicationProtocol)
| project TimeGenerated, SourceHostName, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationPort, ApplicationProtocol, RequestURL
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: msaRAT C2 network connection to known infrastructure

msaRAT WebRTC: debug-launched browser initiating STUN/relay signaling AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts unauthorized WebRTC signaling from a browser that was launched with a remote-debugging port — the msaRAT covert data-channel. Article-specific: Talos recommends behavioral monitoring to catch 'unauthorized WebRTC connections' from the hijacked browser. Rationale: Ties Talos's 'unauthorized WebRTC connections' to concrete STUN/TURN ports (3478/5349) AND the msaRAT-specific pre-condition of a browser started with --remote-debugging-port, so it only fires on hijacked-browser signaling rather than normal video-call WebRTC.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1572
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Teams/Meet/Zoom-in-browser calls using WebRTC STUN on 3478
  • Screen-sharing or WebRTC-based collaboration tools
  • Browser-based softphones (VoIP) that use TURN relays
  • Corporate video conferencing gateways on 5349 (TURN over TLS)
  • WebRTC-based remote-support sessions initiated by helpdesk
Suppression filter
| where RemoteIP == "172.86.126.18" or RemoteIPType == "Public"
Response runbook
1) Triage: verify the browser's launch command line — genuine WebRTC calls are not started via --remote-debugging-port by a non-user parent. Check the STUN/relay destination against 172.86.126.18. 2) Contain: isolate the host, terminate the debug-launched browser, and block the relay endpoint. 3) Hunt: correlate with the CDP launch detection and ProgramData MSI install on the same host; sweep for other endpoints beaconing UDP STUN to the same relay IP.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--remote-debugging-port"
| where Protocol == "Udp"
| where RemotePort in (3478, 3479, 5349, 5350)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteIPType, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where NetworkProtocol has "UDP"
| where DstPortNumber in (3478, 3479, 5349, 5350)
| where DstIpAddr == "172.86.126.18" or (NetworkDirection == "Outbound" and DstIpAddr != "")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, NetworkDirection
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-60137", "CVE-2026-63030")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-60137", "CVE-2026-63030")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-60137", "CVE-2026-63030")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-60137", "CVE-2026-63030")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:

        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'

level: high

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'

        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'

      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "633bd79d1efd3730234d907a2a0d98e3e253a5f0e222e4e4bf3badb3fd6aea0a", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "770dbe473180366d7b539ff2c188e551", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "633bd79d1efd3730234d907a2a0d98e3e253a5f0e222e4e4bf3badb3fd6aea0a", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "770dbe473180366d7b539ff2c188e551", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "633bd79d1efd3730234d907a2a0d98e3e253a5f0e222e4e4bf3badb3fd6aea0a", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "770dbe473180366d7b539ff2c188e551", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "633bd79d1efd3730234d907a2a0d98e3e253a5f0e222e4e4bf3badb3fd6aea0a", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "770dbe473180366d7b539ff2c188e551", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "633bd79d1efd3730234d907a2a0d98e3e253a5f0e222e4e4bf3badb3fd6aea0a", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "770dbe473180366d7b539ff2c188e551", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "633bd79d1efd3730234d907a2a0d98e3e253a5f0e222e4e4bf3badb3fd6aea0a", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "770dbe473180366d7b539ff2c188e551", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a")

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "633bd79d1efd3730234d907a2a0d98e3e253a5f0e222e4e4bf3badb3fd6aea0a", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "770dbe473180366d7b539ff2c188e551", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] UAC-0099 VBS-as-PDF script launched from Public staging dir (Notepad++ chain)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Hackers abuse Notepad++ plugins to stealthily install malware
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Malicious NppExport.dll (LunchPoke) side-loaded by Notepad++ from C:\Users\Public · [LLM] Scheduled task created by Notepad++/loader in C:\Users\Public context (LunchPoke/MatchBoil persistence) · [LLM] WinRAR extracting updater.rar → BurnyBear (RemoteLibUpdater.exe) loader execution · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] UAC-0099 delivery/C2 egress: script host or loader reaching filemail/imageurlgenerator staging · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] BurnyBear resource-exhaustion fallback: process-spawn burst from Public-path loader
UAC-0099 VBS-as-PDF script launched from Public staging dir (Notepad++ chain) AIDelivery High
Hunts wscript/cscript executing a file that carries a .pdf name (double-extension lure) or runs out of the campaign's staging path C:\Users\Public\Temp Documents\. This is UAC-0099's revised delivery: a ZIP with a VBScript disguised as a PDF ('Заводський район.pdf' = 10,559-byte VBScript Script File). Rationale: Uses the exact lure mechanic (VBScript named *.pdf) and the concrete staging path C:\Users\Public\Temp Documents\ read directly from the CERT-UA email/VBS screenshot; script host executing a .pdf-named file is near-zero in normal use. Cross-checked against: • https://socprime.com/blog/detect-uac-0099-attacks-against-ukraine/ • https://securityaffairs.com/180896/apt/cert-ua-warns-of-uac-0099-phishing-attacks-targeting-ukraines-defense-sector.html • https://www.bleepstatic.com/images/news/u/1220909/2026/July/email(1).jpg
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legit admin VBS deployment scripts that happen to reference a PDF report path
  • Software packaging tools staging installers under C:\Users\Public
  • Backup/AV utilities invoking cscript against report files
  • Rare LOB apps that generate PDFs via a wrapper .vbs
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Program Files\" and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full command line and the actual file — confirm the .pdf is really VBScript (check file magic / size ~10.5KB) and note the parent (archiver/browser/mail). 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the wscript/cscript tree, and quarantine anything under C:\Users\Public\Libs_* and C:\Users\Public\Temp Documents\. 3) Hunt: search the same host for notepad++.exe launched from C:\Users\Public, Evernote.zip drops, and outbound to filemail.com / cdn.imageurlgenerator.com.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has ".pdf" or ProcessCommandLine has @"\Users\Public\Temp Documents\"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "wscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "cscript.exe"
| where CommandLine has ".pdf" or CommandLine has @"\Users\Public\Temp Documents\"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Malicious NppExport.dll (LunchPoke) side-loaded by Notepad++ from C:\Users\Public AIInstallation High
Detects the legitimate Notepad++ 8.8.3 binary running from the campaign's random Public directory (C:\Users\Public\Libs_*\Notepad) or spawned by a script host, loading NppExport.dll (LunchPoke) via the plugin mechanism. Notepad++ never installs to C:\Users\Public, so a plugin DLL loaded from there is the side-load. Rationale: NppExport.dll is a real Notepad++ plugin name, so the discriminator is the non-standard load path (C:\Users\Public\Libs_*\Notepad from the VBS) — a legit install lives in Program Files or %AppData%. Sentinel lacks image-load telemetry, so its query pivots on notepad++.exe launched from Public / by a script host instead. Cross-checked against: • https://socprime.com/blog/detect-uac-0099-attacks-against-ukraine/ • https://gbhackers.com/uac-0099-hackers-weaponize-hta-files/ • https://www.bleepstatic.com/images/news/u/1220909/2026/July/email(1).jpg
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Portable Notepad++ run from a USB/temp folder by a developer
  • IT deploying Notepad++ to a shared C:\Users\Public location as a 'portable' app
  • Security researcher detonating samples on an analyst workstation
  • Legit plugin update copying NppExport.dll to a user-writable dir
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has @"\Program Files\Notepad++\" or FolderPath has @"\AppData\Roaming\Notepad++\plugins\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: hash NppExport.dll and the notepad++.exe copy; compare the DLL hash to the known-good plugin and confirm the parent chain (wscript → notepad++). 2) Contain: isolate host, terminate notepad++.exe, quarantine the whole C:\Users\Public\Libs_* directory including updater.rar. 3) Hunt: look for a scheduled task created shortly after this load, and for RemoteLibUpdater.exe / InitTest.dll extraction on the same host.
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "notepad++.exe"
| where FileName =~ "NppExport.dll"
| where FolderPath has @"\Users\Public\" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Users\Public\"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "notepad++.exe"
| where NewProcessName has @"\Users\Public\" or ParentProcessName endswith "wscript.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "cscript.exe"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Scheduled task created by Notepad++/loader in C:\Users\Public context (LunchPoke/MatchBoil persistence) AIInstallation High
Alerts on schtasks.exe /create (or task registration) whose initiating process is notepad++.exe, rundll32.exe, or RemoteLibUpdater.exe, or that runs from C:\Users\Public. Both LunchPoke and MatchBoil V2 establish persistence by creating scheduled tasks from this abnormal context. Rationale: notepad++.exe or a Public-path binary spawning schtasks.exe /create is behaviourally impossible for the real editor; ties LunchPoke's and MatchBoil's stated persistence to a concrete parent→child pair from the article. Cross-checked against: • https://socprime.com/blog/detect-uac-0099-attacks-against-ukraine/ • https://gbhackers.com/uac-0099-hackers-weaponize-hta-files/
ATT&CKT1053.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • rundll32.exe legitimately used by an MSI installer that also registers a task
  • Sysadmin RMM tool wrapping schtasks under a Public working dir
  • Software updaters (e.g. auto-update helpers) creating tasks via rundll32
  • GPO/SCCM deployment invoking schtasks in atypical context
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Program Files\" and InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "rundll32.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: dump the created task's action (binary path + args) and the initiating process tree; note whether the task points at C:\Users\Public. 2) Contain: disable/delete the task (schtasks /delete), isolate the host, and preserve the task XML for IR. 3) Hunt: enumerate all tasks on the host referencing Public paths, and pivot to RemoteLibUpdater.exe execution and outbound C2 to correlate the MatchBoil stage.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/create"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("notepad++.exe","rundll32.exe","RemoteLibUpdater.exe") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Users\Public\"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4698
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| where EventData has @"\Users\Public\" or EventData has "notepad++.exe" or EventData has "RemoteLibUpdater.exe"
| extend TaskName = extract("<TaskName>(.*?)</TaskName>", 1, tostring(EventData))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, TaskName, EventData
| order by TimeGenerated desc

WinRAR extracting updater.rar → BurnyBear (RemoteLibUpdater.exe) loader execution AIInstallation High
Detects the legitimate WinRAR bundled in the archive extracting the password-protected updater.rar, and/or execution of the extracted RemoteLibUpdater.exe (BurnyBear), which side-loads InitTest.dll (MatchBoil V2). Targets the named binaries so it fires on the exact tooling in the chain. Rationale: RemoteLibUpdater.exe and updater.rar are attack-specific names from CERT-UA; RemoteLibUpdater.exe is not a real Microsoft/third-party binary, so any execution is high-fidelity, and the winrar+updater.rar pair pins the extraction step. Cross-checked against: • https://socprime.com/blog/detect-uac-0099-attacks-against-ukraine/ • https://medium.com/h7w/updated-uac-0099-toolkit-matchboil-matchwok-dragstare-cc9e28acbde3
ATT&CKT1105 T1204.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A benign internal tool coincidentally named RemoteLibUpdater.exe (rare; verify signer)
  • User manually extracting an unrelated archive literally named updater.rar
  • Red-team/adversary-emulation reusing these public IOC names
  • WinRAR self-extractor with a similar arg pattern
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture RemoteLibUpdater.exe + InitTest.dll hashes and signer, and the WinRAR command line (look for -p/-hp password flag against updater.rar). 2) Contain: isolate host, kill the loader, quarantine updater.rar + extracted payloads under C:\Users\Public. 3) Hunt: check for the MatchBoil-created second scheduled task, C2 beaconing with an 'SN' HTTP header, and any resource-exhaustion fallback child-spawn burst.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName =~ "RemoteLibUpdater.exe")
    or (FileName =~ "winrar.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "updater.rar")
    or (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "winrar.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "RemoteLibUpdater")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "RemoteLibUpdater.exe"
    or (NewProcessName endswith "winrar.exe" and CommandLine has "updater.rar")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

BurnyBear resource-exhaustion fallback: process-spawn burst from Public-path loader AIActions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection for BurnyBear's stated fallback — when RemoteLibUpdater.exe fails to launch it triggers a RAM/CPU resource-exhaustion attack. Surfaces a burst of >50 child processes per minute from RemoteLibUpdater.exe/BurnyBear or any binary running from C:\Users\Public. Rationale: Encodes BurnyBear's explicitly-described fallback (RAM/CPU exhaustion on RemoteLibUpdater.exe launch failure) as a per-minute child-spawn burst keyed to the named loader / Public path; no Sigma emitted because this is a threshold/aggregation, not a single-event shape. Cross-checked against: • https://gbhackers.com/uac-0099-hackers-weaponize-hta-files/ • https://medium.com/h7w/updated-uac-0099-toolkit-matchboil-matchwok-dragstare-cc9e28acbde3
ATT&CKT1499.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Build/CI agent under C:\Users\Public spawning many compiler processes
  • Legit batch job or script fan-out from a shared Public working dir
  • Antivirus full-scan helper spawning many short-lived scan procs
  • Software installer that recursively launches many helper processes
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("msbuild.exe","cl.exe","conhost.exe","MsMpEng.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the burst parent is RemoteLibUpdater.exe or a Public-path binary and correlate with host CPU/RAM saturation; check the loader's exit code just before the burst. 2) Contain: isolate host, kill the parent tree, and cap the runaway processes to restore availability. 3) Hunt: verify whether the primary MatchBoil stage failed (the trigger), and sweep other hosts for RemoteLibUpdater.exe launch failures followed by spawn bursts.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("RemoteLibUpdater.exe","BurnyBear.exe") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Users\Public\"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize ChildCount = count(), DistinctChildren = dcount(FileName), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), SampleChild = any(ProcessCommandLine)
    by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where ChildCount > 50    // >50 child procs/min from the loader = fork-bomb style resource exhaustion
| order by ChildCount desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "RemoteLibUpdater.exe" or ParentProcessName has @"\Users\Public\"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| summarize ChildCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer, ParentProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where ChildCount > 50    // fork-bomb style resource exhaustion fallback
| order by ChildCount desc
source:windows.security @EventID:4688 (@ParentImage:(*\\RemoteLibUpdater.exe OR *\\remotelibupdater.exe) OR @ParentImage:(*\\Users\\Public\\* OR *\\users\\public\\*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/RemoteLibUpdater\.exe/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RawProcessId], function=count(as=child_count))
| child_count > 50
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("RemoteLibUpdater.exe","BurnyBear.exe") OR Processes.parent_process_path="*\\Users\\Public\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process_id _time span=1m 
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` 
| where count > 50 
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("RemoteLibUpdater.exe","BurnyBear.exe") OR Processes.parent_process_path="*\\Users\\Public\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process_id _time span=1m 
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` 
| where count > 50 
| sort - count
UAC-0099 delivery/C2 egress: script host or loader reaching filemail/imageurlgenerator staging AICommand & Control Medium
Flags outbound connections to the campaign's staging/C2 infrastructure (2111.filemail.com, cdn.imageurlgenerator.com, easysend.co, cutt.ly) initiated by wscript/cscript/notepad++/RemoteLibUpdater. The VBS pulls the disguised PDF from filemail and Evernote.zip from cdn.imageurlgenerator.com. Rationale: Domains pulled from the VBS body in the CERT-UA email screenshot (2111.filemail.com/api/file/get, cdn.imageurlgenerator.com/uploads/*.txt, cutt.ly→easysend.co redirect); scoping to script-host/loader initiators cuts the FP from these being shared file-transfer/URL-shortener services. Sentinel query is DNS-only (no process attribution in DnsEvents), so pair with a process pivot on hit. Cross-checked against: • https://securityaffairs.com/180896/apt/cert-ua-warns-of-uac-0099-phishing-attacks-targeting-ukraines-defense-sector.html • https://www.bleepstatic.com/images/news/u/1220909/2026/July/email(1).jpg
ATT&CKT1105 T1071.001 T1102
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Users legitimately downloading files via filemail.com or clicking cutt.ly links
  • Marketing/design staff using imageurlgenerator or easysend for file sharing
  • Browser prefetch/telemetry resolving these domains without a real transfer
  • Security tooling detonating URLs from the same shorteners
Suppression filter
DeviceNetworkEvents | where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","outlook.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: on a hit, immediately pivot to the initiating process — a script host or notepad++ reaching filemail/imageurlgenerator is malicious; a browser is likely benign. 2) Contain: block the four domains at the proxy/DNS, isolate any host where a non-browser process made the request, and pull the downloaded artifact. 3) Hunt: search the same host for the full chain (VBS-as-PDF, notepad++ from Public, RemoteLibUpdater.exe) and check for MatchBoil beaconing with an 'SN' header.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("filemail.com","cdn.imageurlgenerator.com","easysend.co","cutt.ly")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","notepad++.exe","RemoteLibUpdater.exe","powershell.exe","mshta.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Name has_any ("filemail.com","cdn.imageurlgenerator.com","easysend.co","cutt.ly")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] FakeAgent: ClaudeDesktop.exe execution + tampered libcef.dll side-load (SectopRAT) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] npm postinstall dropper spawns osascript (AMOS macOS stealer via @copilot-mcp/apex) · [LLM] FakeAgent SectopRAT persistence: DockerDesktop.exe scheduled task + Defender exclusion · Suspicious browser extension installation · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] AMOS stealer exfil staging /tmp/osalogging.zip + LaunchAgent C2 persistence (macOS) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
npm postinstall dropper spawns osascript (AMOS macOS stealer via @copilot-mcp/apex) AIInstallation High
Hunts a Node/npm process tree spawning osascript on macOS, the exact second-stage behaviour of the @copilot-mcp/apex and @apexfdn/apex droppers that decrypt and run an AMOS-family AppleScript payload. Legitimate npm installs almost never spawn osascript, making the parent→child pair high-fidelity. Rationale: Anchors on the article's stated chain (npm install/npx @copilot-mcp/apex -> osascript AppleScript payload). Corroborated by Microsoft and SOC Prime macOS-stealer write-ups that flag node->osascript as the AMOS delivery signature. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/02/02/infostealers-without-borders-macos-python-stealers-and-platform-abuse/ • https://socprime.com/active-threats/macos-stealers-observed-what-defenders-should-watch-for/
ATT&CKT1059.002 T1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate npm package that uses osascript to prompt for permissions during postinstall (rare, e.g. some GUI-integration tooling)
  • Developer manually testing an AppleScript build step from a Node script
  • Electron/Node tooling that shells out to osascript to display native macOS notifications
  • Homebrew Node formula post-install scripts invoking osascript for UI
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install","npx","@copilot-mcp/apex","@apexfdn/apex") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("decrypt","base64","do shell script","curl","osalogging")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full osascript command line and the initiating npm/npx command; look for base64, gunzip, curl, JXA, or a decrypt routine in the AppleScript body and check for a package name matching @copilot-mcp/apex or @apexfdn/apex. 2) Contain: isolate the macOS host, kill the osascript/node chain, and revoke any AWS/Kubernetes/SSH creds and browser/crypto-wallet secrets that were on-disk (this stealer harvests them). 3) Hunt: search the same host and package registry usage across the fleet for /tmp/osalogging.zip and LaunchAgents polling a C2, and audit which developers ran that package.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "osascript"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","npm","npx","node.js") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npx ","postinstall","@copilot-mcp/apex","@apexfdn/apex")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "osascript"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","npm","npx","node.js") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npx ","postinstall","@copilot-mcp/apex","@apexfdn/apex")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by TimeGenerated desc

AMOS stealer exfil staging /tmp/osalogging.zip + LaunchAgent C2 persistence (macOS) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts creation of the AMOS stealer's fixed exfil archive /tmp/osalogging.zip and/or a LaunchAgent plist written alongside osascript/curl activity that polls the C2 every 60 seconds. These are hardcoded artefacts of the @copilot-mcp/apex payload, giving a near-zero-FP alert. Rationale: Uses two fixed article strings: the /tmp/osalogging.zip staging archive and the LaunchAgent that polls C2 every 60s. The zip path is a literal, near-unique IOC; the LaunchAgent+osascript pairing is corroborated by Microsoft/SOC Prime AMOS persistence analysis. Cross-checked against: • https://socprime.com/active-threats/macos-stealers-observed-what-defenders-should-watch-for/ • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/02/02/infostealers-without-borders-macos-python-stealers-and-platform-abuse/
ATT&CKT1074.001 T1543.001 T1041
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer or backup tool coincidentally naming a zip 'osalogging.zip' (extremely unlikely)
  • Legitimate app writing a LaunchAgent that shells out to curl for update checks
  • Corporate MDM deploying a LaunchAgent for telemetry (whitelist the MDM signing process)
  • Security tooling itself staging archives in /tmp during testing
Suppression filter
| where FileName =~ "osalogging.zip" or (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "osascript" and FolderPath has "/Library/LaunchAgents/")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the writing process (should be osascript or a Node-descended shell); pull the LaunchAgent plist and read its ProgramArguments for the C2 URL and 60s polling loop. 2) Contain: isolate the host, delete the LaunchAgent and quarantine the payload, and force-rotate every credential class the stealer targets (browser, 20+ crypto wallets, SSH, AWS, Kubernetes, login Keychain, Telegram). 3) Hunt: pivot on the C2 host from the plist across DNS/proxy logs, and sweep for node->osascript execution (see companion UC) to find the initial dropper.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName =~ "osalogging.zip")
    or (FolderPath has "/Library/LaunchAgents/" and ActionType == "FileCreated" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("osascript","curl","/tmp/"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
DeviceFileEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (FileName =~ "osalogging.zip")
    or (FolderPath has "/Library/LaunchAgents/" and ActionType == "FileCreated" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("osascript","curl","/tmp/"))
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

FakeAgent: ClaudeDesktop.exe execution + tampered libcef.dll side-load (SectopRAT) AIDelivery High
Hunts the FakeAgent malvertising payload — a fake ClaudeDesktop.exe downloaded from an attacker site (via a Claude.ai artifact redirect) that runs a renamed signed JetBrains binary to side-load a tampered libcef.dll carrying SectopRAT. Targets both the named lure binary and the DLL-sideload-from-staging-dir behaviour. Rationale: ClaudeDesktop.exe is the article's named lure binary (the genuine app ships as Claude.exe). Huntress corroboration adds the tampered libcef.dll side-load loaded from a user-writable staging dir, which the DeviceImageLoadEvents leg catches even if the lure binary is renamed. Cross-checked against: • https://www.huntress.com/blog/fakeagent-claude-desktop-malvertising-ends-in-dotnet-rat • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/07/23/anthropic-claude-artifacts-download-malware/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1204.002 T1583.008
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine Claude desktop app (ships as Claude.exe, not ClaudeDesktop.exe) — name mismatch keeps FP low
  • Legitimate CEF/Electron apps (Spotify, Steam, portable browsers) loading libcef.dll from install dirs — excluded by the staging-dir path filter
  • A portable/dev build of a real app run from Downloads that legitimately carries libcef.dll
  • Internal software repackaging that stages CEF apps in Temp during MSI extraction
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Program Files\", @"\Program Files (x86)\") and Signal == "libcef.dll side-load from staging dir")
Response runbook
1) Triage: verify the ClaudeDesktop.exe path/hash against the genuine Claude.exe; inspect the process that loaded libcef.dll for a valid JetBrains signature but an out-of-place folder (Downloads/Temp), and check for VMProtect packing and a GPU/graphics-hardware check (anti-VM). 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the process tree, quarantine the ClaudeDesktop.exe bundle and tampered libcef.dll, and block the attacker download domain. 3) Hunt: pivot to the companion DockerDesktop.exe scheduled-task/Defender-exclusion UC, review Bing/ad-referred downloads across the fleet, and check for SectopRAT credit-card/credential exfil beacons.
let ClaudeLure = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "ClaudeDesktop.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Signal="ClaudeDesktop.exe execution", Path=FolderPath, Cmd=ProcessCommandLine, SHA256;
let LibcefSideload = DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "libcef.dll"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Signal="libcef.dll side-load from staging dir", Path=FolderPath, Cmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256=InitiatingProcessSHA256;
union ClaudeLure, LibcefSideload
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\ClaudeDesktop.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

FakeAgent SectopRAT persistence: DockerDesktop.exe scheduled task + Defender exclusion AIInstallation High
Hunts the FakeAgent post-exploitation persistence — a dropped DockerDesktop.exe registered as a scheduled task, plus Add-MpPreference Defender exclusions the operator sets to protect the payload. Both are hardcoded behaviours Huntress observed across the 29 victim organizations. Rationale: DockerDesktop.exe as a scheduled-task persistence binary (genuine Docker Desktop ships as 'Docker Desktop.exe' with a space, in Program Files) plus Add-MpPreference exclusions are the two persistence/evasion steps Huntress documented for FakeAgent; both are user-context, non-machine-account actions. Cross-checked against: • https://www.huntress.com/blog/fakeagent-claude-desktop-malvertising-ends-in-dotnet-rat • https://www.itsecurityguru.org/2026/07/23/fakeagent-campaign-malicious-claude-artifact-used-to-distribute-sectoprat-to-29-organisations/
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine Docker Desktop install task ('Docker Desktop.exe' with space, under Program Files) — the no-space DockerDesktop.exe token reduces overlap
  • Endpoint/AV admin legitimately adding a Defender exclusion via Add-MpPreference during troubleshooting
  • EDR or software-deployment tooling registering scheduled tasks under SYSTEM (filtered by machine-account exclusion)
  • A developer scripting Register-ScheduledTask for a personal automation named 'Docker...'
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("gpscript.exe","msiexec.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has @"\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: dump the scheduled-task action path/hash for DockerDesktop.exe (confirm it's in a user-writable dir, not Program Files) and enumerate any Defender exclusions added around the same time (Get-MpPreference) to see what the operator is protecting. 2) Contain: isolate the host, delete the rogue task, remove the exclusion, and quarantine DockerDesktop.exe and the associated ClaudeDesktop.exe/libcef.dll bundle. 3) Hunt: sweep the fleet for the same DockerDesktop.exe task name and identical exclusion paths, and correlate to the FakeAgent delivery UC (ClaudeDesktop.exe / libcef.dll side-load).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where (FileName =~ "schtasks.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("/create","DockerDesktop.exe"))
    or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("Register-ScheduledTask","DockerDesktop"))
    or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "Add-MpPreference" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-ExclusionPath","-ExclusionProcess"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where not(SubjectUserName endswith "$")
| where (NewProcessName endswith "\\schtasks.exe" and CommandLine has "/create" and CommandLine has "DockerDesktop.exe")
    or (NewProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and CommandLine has "Add-MpPreference" and CommandLine has_any ("-ExclusionPath","-ExclusionProcess"))
    or (NewProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and CommandLine has "Register-ScheduledTask" and CommandLine has "DockerDesktop")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: FakeAgent SectopRAT persistence via DockerDesktop.exe task or Defender exclusion
id: c81f5a67-2b90-4e13-8d6c-9f0a4b7e5d22
description: Detects the FakeAgent campaign persistence steps - registering a dropped DockerDesktop.exe as a scheduled task or adding a Microsoft Defender exclusion via Add-MpPreference
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/threatsday-android-spyware-plc-attacks.html
  - https://www.huntress.com/blog/fakeagent-claude-desktop-malvertising-ends-in-dotnet-rat
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/23
tags:
  - attack.t1053.005
  - attack.t1562.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  sel_task:
    Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/create'
      - 'DockerDesktop.exe'
  sel_defender:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'Add-MpPreference'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-ExclusionPath'
      - '-ExclusionProcess'
  condition: sel_task or sel_defender
level: high
source:windows.security @EventID:4688 ((@Image:(*\\schtasks.exe OR *\\SCHTASKS.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*DockerDesktop.exe* AND */create*)) OR (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe) AND @CommandLine:*Add-MpPreference* AND @CommandLine:(*-ExclusionPath* OR *-ExclusionProcess*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (ImageFileName=/\\schtasks\.exe$/i CommandLine=/\/create/i CommandLine=/DockerDesktop\.exe/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i CommandLine=/Add-MpPreference/i CommandLine=/(ExclusionPath|ExclusionProcess)/i)
| table([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine])
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=schtasks.exe AND Processes.process="*DockerDesktop.exe*" AND Processes.process="*/create*") OR (Processes.process_name IN (powershell.exe,pwsh.exe) AND Processes.process="*Add-MpPreference*" AND Processes.process="*Exclusion*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=schtasks.exe AND Processes.process="*DockerDesktop.exe*" AND Processes.process="*/create*") OR (Processes.process_name IN (powershell.exe,pwsh.exe) AND Processes.process="*Add-MpPreference*" AND Processes.process="*Exclusion*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"

| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
