| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |

    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Inbound phishing from ClickUp/pixeldrain malware campaign sender 9i6pokerdepot.com · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Email threat landscape: Q2 2026 trends and insights
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] BAT dropper / pixeldrain installer written to disk (Financial_report.bat, Temp installer.exe) · [LLM] Financial_report.bat spawning hidden PowerShell to pull installer.exe from pixeldrain · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Endpoint egress to ClickUp stage-2 dropper subdomain and pixeldrain payload host · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Inbound phishing from ClickUp/pixeldrain malware campaign sender 9i6pokerdepot.com AIDelivery High
Hunts inbound mail from the Q2-2026 multi-stage malware campaign's DKIM-signed sender domain 9i6pokerdepot.com (Customer.Service@9i6pokerdepot.com). These messages carried a Microsoft-auth-redirect link that ultimately fetched a ClickUp-hosted BAT dropper. Article-specific because it keys on the exact operator sending domain, not generic phishing heuristics. Rationale: Keys on the exact campaign sender domain/address from the article IOC table (9i6pokerdepot.com, Customer.Service@9i6pokerdepot.com, DKIM-signed by operator) — a fixed operator-controlled string, so any inbound hit is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/07/23/email-threat-landscape-q2-2026-trends-and-insights/ • https://dslua.org/publications/analysis-report-targeted-phishing-attack-leading-to-remote-access-trojan-deployment/
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1656
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate business genuinely registers 9i6pokerdepot.com later and emails an employee (unlikely — throwaway gambling-themed domain)
  • Internal phishing-simulation platform spoofing this sender for awareness training
  • Security researcher forwarding a sample of the campaign into a monitored mailbox
  • Threat-intel enrichment/detonation service replaying the message
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull all EmailEvents for SenderFromDomain 9i6pokerdepot.com, note RecipientEmailAddress list and DeliveryAction (Delivered vs Blocked); check AuthenticationDetails for the DKIM pass the operator self-signed. 2) Contain: soft-delete/purge delivered copies tenant-wide via Explorer, block the domain at mailflow, and add 9i6pokerdepot.com to the tenant block list. 3) Hunt: for each recipient who received it, pivot to UC2/UC3/UC4 (clickup-attachments subdomain, pixeldrain download, Financial_report.bat execution) on their device to confirm whether the chain progressed past delivery.
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
| where SenderFromDomain =~ "9i6pokerdepot.com" or SenderMailFromDomain =~ "9i6pokerdepot.com" or SenderFromAddress =~ "Customer.Service@9i6pokerdepot.com"
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderMailFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation, AuthenticationDetails
| order by Timestamp desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
EmailEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
| where SenderFromDomain =~ "9i6pokerdepot.com" or SenderMailFromDomain =~ "9i6pokerdepot.com" or SenderFromAddress =~ "Customer.Service@9i6pokerdepot.com"
| project TimeGenerated, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderMailFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation, AuthenticationDetails
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Email.All_Email where All_Email.direction="inbound" AND (All_Email.src_user="Customer.Service@9i6pokerdepot.com" OR All_Email.src_user="*@9i6pokerdepot.com") by All_Email.src_user All_Email.recipient All_Email.subject All_Email.message_id | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Email.All_Email where All_Email.direction="inbound" AND (All_Email.src_user="Customer.Service@9i6pokerdepot.com" OR All_Email.src_user="*@9i6pokerdepot.com") by All_Email.src_user All_Email.recipient All_Email.subject All_Email.message_id | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Endpoint egress to ClickUp stage-2 dropper subdomain and pixeldrain payload host AICommand & Control High
Hunts device connections/DNS to the campaign's stage-2 hosting infrastructure: the unique ClickUp attachment subdomain t90141296286.p.clickup-attachments.com serving the BAT dropper, and pixeldrain.com serving the final installer.exe. Article-specific because it keys on the exact operator subdomain plus the file-sharing host abused for the final stage. Rationale: t90141296286.p.clickup-attachments.com is a unique operator-controlled subdomain from the IOC table (stage-2 BAT host); pixeldrain.com is corroborated by multiple ANY.RUN detonations of this chain as the final installer host — rare enough in enterprise egress to alert on. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/07/23/email-threat-landscape-q2-2026-trends-and-insights/ • https://any.run/report/84f73741867e012140103aa9eb59bfaef6bf8c02aa7b9579be7aad2143418c03/18abf34d-1f07-4902-8343-13b9f8358605 • https://dslua.org/publications/analysis-report-targeted-phishing-attack-leading-to-remote-access-trojan-deployment/
ATT&CKT1105 T1102 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate ClickUp customer downloading a genuine attachment (but NOT from the t90141296286 tenant subdomain — that clause is campaign-unique)
  • Developer/user legitimately sharing a large file via pixeldrain.com
  • Security analyst detonating the sample and reaching the same infra
  • Web-proxy/URL-rewrite service pre-fetching the link on the user's behalf
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe") and RemoteUrl has "pixeldrain.com" and RemoteUrl !has "3v92oJiL")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the InitiatingProcessFileName that made the connection — a browser is lower-severity delivery; powershell.exe/cmd.exe/curl.exe is active payload retrieval (escalate). Confirm whether the t90141296286 subdomain (BAT stage) or pixeldrain (final stage) was reached. 2) Contain: block both hosts at the proxy/firewall/DNS, and network-isolate any device that reached pixeldrain (final installer stage). 3) Hunt: on that device pivot to DeviceFileEvents for installer.exe/Financial_report.bat (UC3) and DeviceProcessEvents for the hidden-PowerShell chain (UC4) to establish execution.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("t90141296286.p.clickup-attachments.com", "pixeldrain.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery has_any ("t90141296286.p.clickup-attachments.com", "pixeldrain.com")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

BAT dropper / pixeldrain installer written to disk (Financial_report.bat, Temp installer.exe) AIInstallation High
Hunts the on-disk artifacts of the campaign: the ClickUp-delivered Financial_report.bat dropper and the installer.exe pulled from pixeldrain into the user Temp directory, or any file whose download origin URL is the ClickUp/pixeldrain infrastructure. Article-specific via the exact filenames and origin hosts corroborated by external analysis. Rationale: Financial_report.bat and the Temp-dropped installer.exe are the corroborated (dslua/ANY.RUN) on-disk names; the FileOriginUrl clause anchors to the article's clickup-attachments/pixeldrain hosts so it fires even if the operator rotates filenames. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/07/23/email-threat-landscape-q2-2026-trends-and-insights/ • https://dslua.org/publications/analysis-report-targeted-phishing-attack-leading-to-remote-access-trojan-deployment/ • https://any.run/report/0668dca5f990f738119e65afa63129ac2eacff12762a45b4129355ba340f218a/13a43921-af25-4d00-b578-bb72ce371788
ATT&CKT1105 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate app installer named installer.exe extracting itself to %Temp% (very common — the FileOriginUrl/pixeldrain clause is what disambiguates)
  • In-house automation batch file coincidentally named Financial_report.bat
  • Backup/EDR tooling staging files in Temp
  • Analyst manually saving the sample to Temp during investigation
Suppression filter
| where FileOriginUrl has_any ("clickup-attachments.com","pixeldrain.com") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","msedge.exe","chrome.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the write's FileOriginUrl points to clickup-attachments/pixeldrain (true positive) vs a benign local installer; capture SHA256 and submit to sandbox/AV. 2) Contain: quarantine the file, isolate the host if installer.exe already executed, and reset the user's credentials given the phishing origin. 3) Hunt: pivot to DeviceProcessEvents (UC4) for the hidden-PowerShell → pixeldrain chain and self-deletion of the dropper, and check DeviceNetworkEvents (UC2) for any post-install C2 from the machine.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileOriginUrl has_any ("clickup-attachments.com", "pixeldrain.com/api/file", "3v92oJiL"))
    or (FileName =~ "Financial_report.bat")
    or (FileName =~ "installer.exe" and FolderPath has @"\Temp\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, FileOriginUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileName =~ "Financial_report.bat"
    or (TargetFileName =~ "installer.exe" and TargetFilePath has @"\Temp\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Financial_report.bat spawning hidden PowerShell to pull installer.exe from pixeldrain AIInstallation High
Hunts the execution stage: the ClickUp-delivered Financial_report.bat launching a hidden PowerShell that downloads installer.exe from pixeldrain.com/api/file into Temp, runs it silently, then self-deletes the dropper. Article-specific via the exact pixeldrain file id 3v92oJiL and corroborated BAT filename plus hidden-window + self-delete behaviour. Rationale: pixeldrain.com/api/file/3v92oJiL is the exact final-payload URL from the article IOC table and 3v92oJiL is a unique file id; the Financial_report.bat parent and script-host download behaviour are corroborated by external analysis — combining them yields near-zero-FP execution-stage coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/07/23/email-threat-landscape-q2-2026-trends-and-insights/ • https://dslua.org/publications/analysis-report-targeted-phishing-attack-leading-to-remote-access-trojan-deployment/ • https://any.run/report/84f73741867e012140103aa9eb59bfaef6bf8c02aa7b9579be7aad2143418c03/18abf34d-1f07-4902-8343-13b9f8358605
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.003 T1564.003 T1070.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • An analyst reproducing the download command with the pixeldrain URL in a lab
  • A benign internal batch job coincidentally named Financial_report.bat launching a child process
  • Threat-intel automation curling the pixeldrain URL for enrichment
  • Red-team exercise replaying this specific chain
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !endswith "$" and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("code.exe","pwsh.exe") and AccountName has "analyst")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the command line contains the pixeldrain file id 3v92oJiL / api/file path and note whether installer.exe was written and executed from Temp; capture parent Financial_report.bat and child hashes. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the process tree, block pixeldrain.com and the ClickUp subdomain, and reset the affected user. 3) Hunt: recover the self-deleted BAT via DeviceFileEvents (UC3), check for the installer.exe process's follow-on network (UC2) and any persistence (Run keys/scheduled tasks) it created, then sweep other recipients of the 9i6pokerdepot.com mail (UC1).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","curl.exe","bitsadmin.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("pixeldrain.com/api/file","3v92oJiL"))
    or (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "Financial_report.bat")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","curl.exe","bitsadmin.exe") and CommandLine has_any ("pixeldrain.com/api/file","3v92oJiL"))
    or (CommandLine has "Financial_report.bat" or ParentProcessName has "Financial_report.bat")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: pixeldrain payload download via script host (ClickUp BAT dropper chain)
id: c3d8f5b1-2a49-4e0c-b7f6-9d61a4e08c72
description: Detects a Windows script host referencing the pixeldrain payload URL/file id, or a process whose parent is Financial_report.bat, in the Q2 2026 Microsoft-auth-redirect malware campaign.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/07/23/email-threat-landscape-q2-2026-trends-and-insights/
  - https://dslua.org/publications/analysis-report-targeted-phishing-attack-leading-to-remote-access-trojan-deployment/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/23
tags:
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_url:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'pixeldrain.com/api/file'
      - '3v92oJiL'
  selection_parent:
    ParentCommandLine|contains: 'Financial_report.bat'
  condition: selection_url or selection_parent
level: high
source:windows.security @EventID:4688 (@CommandLine:(*pixeldrain.com/api/file* OR *3v92oJiL*) OR @CommandLine:(*Financial_report.bat* OR *financial_report.bat*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (CommandLine=/pixeldrain\.com\/api\/file/i OR CommandLine=/3v92oJiL/i OR ParentBaseFileName=/financial_report\.bat/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*pixeldrain.com/api/file*" OR Processes.process="*3v92oJiL*" OR Processes.parent_process="*Financial_report.bat*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*pixeldrain.com/api/file*" OR Processes.process="*3v92oJiL*" OR Processes.parent_process="*Financial_report.bat*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.

Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Auth.js (next-auth v5) server-configuration error surfaced in application logs (fail-open trigger) · [LLM] HTTP 500 on Auth.js /api/auth/session endpoint (@auth/core error body read as session) · Article-specific behavioural hunt — [GHSA / CRITICAL] GHSA-8fpg-xm3f-6cx3: Auth.js: Configuration errors can cause e

Auth.js (next-auth v5) server-configuration error surfaced in application logs (fail-open trigger) AIExploitation High
Hunts the exact Auth.js error signatures that flip existence-based `!!auth` checks to permanently true: `[auth][error]` lines carrying `InvalidEndpoints`, `MissingSecret`/`AUTH_SECRET`, or the user-facing 'There was a problem with the server configuration' message. Presence of any of these in a running next-auth v5 deployment means every request is currently being treated as authenticated. Rationale: Anchored on the exact log strings the advisory prints (`[auth][error] InvalidEndpoints`, `MissingSecret`/`AUTH_SECRET`, and the verbatim config-error message). These are Auth.js-internal error class names (single canonical casing) confirmed in next-auth issues #10538/#11934, so false positives are essentially limited to intentionally-misconfigured non-prod. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8fpg-xm3f-6cx3 • https://cvereports.com/reports/GHSA-8FPG-XM3F-6CX3 • https://github.com/nextauthjs/next-auth/issues/11934 • https://github.com/nextauthjs/next-auth/issues/10538
ATT&CKT1556
Data sourcesApplication error logs (no CIM datamodel covers app-error strings)
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Staging/preview deployments deliberately started without AUTH_SECRET where fail-open is not internet-exposed
  • A one-time deploy that logged the error but the pod was rolled back within seconds (transient, no live exposure)
  • Developer running the app locally with an incomplete provider config
  • Blue-team chaos/DR test intentionally removing an env var to validate this very alert
  • Log-forwarding replay/backfill re-ingesting historical error lines from before the patch
Suppression filter
| where not(Computer has_any ("staging","preview","dev","-qa"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the host/app emitting `[auth][error]` and confirm it is a production, internet-facing next-auth v5 (>=5.0.0-beta.0, <=5.0.0-beta.31) deployment; if so it is fail-open RIGHT NOW. 2) Contain: restore the missing config (AUTH_SECRET / provider issuer) or take the route/app offline, then upgrade to next-auth@beta and switch middleware checks to `!!req.auth?.user`. 3) Hunt: pull all HTTP access to protected routes since the first error timestamp and review for unauthenticated access that succeeded (feed into the correlation UC).
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where SyslogMessage has "[auth][error]"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("InvalidEndpoints","MissingSecret","AUTH_SECRET","There was a problem with the server configuration")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Auth.js next-auth v5 Server-Configuration Error (Fail-Open Condition)
id: 3f8b1d2a-9c44-4e77-8a1c-2b6f0e5d7a91
status: experimental
description: Detects Auth.js/@auth/core server-configuration error log lines that cause existence-based auth checks (!!auth) to fail open per GHSA-8fpg-xm3f-6cx3.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8fpg-xm3f-6cx3
  - https://github.com/nextauthjs/next-auth/issues/11934
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/23
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1556
logsource:
  category: application
  product: nodejs
detection:
  prefix:
    Message|contains: '[auth][error]'
  errortype:
    Message|contains:
      - 'InvalidEndpoints'
      - 'MissingSecret'
      - 'AUTH_SECRET'
      - 'There was a problem with the server configuration'
  condition: prefix and errortype
falsepositives:
  - Non-production/staging deployments intentionally started without AUTH_SECRET
level: high
source:nodejs "[auth][error]" (InvalidEndpoints OR MissingSecret OR AUTH_SECRET OR "There was a problem with the server configuration")
APPLICATION
index=* sourcetype IN ("nodejs","nextjs","node:application") ("[auth][error]") ("InvalidEndpoints" OR "MissingSecret" OR "AUTH_SECRET" OR "There was a problem with the server configuration") | stats count AS hits, min(_time) AS firstSeen, max(_time) AS lastSeen, values(source) AS sources BY host | sort - hits
HTTP 500 on Auth.js /api/auth/session endpoint (@auth/core error body read as session) AIExploitation Medium
Detects the wire-level trigger of the fail-open: the next-auth wrapper calls @auth/core's /api/auth/session, which returns HTTP 500 with a JSON error body that the wrapper reads via response.json() without checking status, populating a truthy `auth` object. A cluster of 500s on /api/auth/* on a next-auth deployment indicates active fail-open exposure. Rationale: Uses the confirmed root-cause mechanism (from CVEReports and issue #11934): @auth/core returns 500 on /api/auth/session and the wrapper reads the body as a session. The endpoint path `/api/auth/session` is the Auth.js default, so the URI+status pair is deployment-agnostic and directly maps to the bypass trigger. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8fpg-xm3f-6cx3 • https://cvereports.com/reports/GHSA-8FPG-XM3F-6CX3 • https://github.com/nextauthjs/next-auth/issues/11934
ATT&CKT1556 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Backend/database outage causing 500s across the whole app, not just auth
  • OAuth provider (Keycloak/Entra) temporary unavailability making token endpoints 500
  • Deploy window where env vars are briefly unset during a rolling restart
  • Load-test / synthetic monitor hammering /api/auth during a maintenance window
  • CDN/edge health-check probes hitting the auth endpoint before warm-up
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the 500s are concentrated on /api/auth/session (not app-wide 500s) and that the target is a next-auth v5 build in the vulnerable beta range. 2) Contain: fix the underlying config error (AUTH_SECRET/provider issuer) or take the app offline; upgrade to next-auth@beta so config errors fail closed. 3) Hunt: correlate these 500 timestamps with successful 2xx/3xx access to protected non-auth routes from the same client IPs to find requests that slipped through fail-open.
AppServiceHTTPLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where CsUriStem startswith "/api/auth"
| where ScStatus == 500
| summarize Count = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Endpoints = make_set(CsUriStem, 20) by CsHost, CIp
| where Count >= 1
| order by Count desc
title: Auth.js @auth/core HTTP 500 on /api/auth Session Endpoint
id: b71e4c58-2a3f-4d90-9e11-7c5a8f2d16e4
status: experimental
description: Detects HTTP 500 responses on the Auth.js /api/auth session endpoint, the wire-level trigger for the GHSA-8fpg-xm3f-6cx3 fail-open where the error body is parsed as a session.

detection:

Auth.js fail-open evidence: successful protected-route access within window of /api/auth 500 error AIActions on Objectives Medium
Correlation that produces the actual bypass evidence: a client that received an HTTP 500 on /api/auth/* (auth layer broken) then successfully loaded a protected non-auth route (200/302) within a short window. This is the observable signature of an unauthenticated visitor being treated as logged-in because the truthy error object satisfied the `if (req.auth)` check. Rationale: Ties the two article-grounded halves together: the 500 on /api/auth (broken auth layer) and a subsequent successful hit on a protected route from the same client — exactly the 'fails open, grants access to everyone' outcome the advisory describes. Static-asset and /_next/ paths are excluded so the surviving hits represent real application routes. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8fpg-xm3f-6cx3 • https://cvereports.com/reports/GHSA-8FPG-XM3F-6CX3
ATT&CKT1556 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A genuinely authenticated user whose session-refresh call (/api/auth/session) 500'd transiently but who already held a valid cookie
  • Shared egress NAT/proxy where an errored client IP and a legitimately-authenticated client IP collapse to the same CIp
  • Public/unauthenticated routes that were never actually gated being matched as 'protected'
  • Retry storms where the browser re-requested the page after the 500 and got a cached 200
  • Monitoring bot that probes both the auth endpoint and app pages from one IP
Suppression filter
| where not(ProtectedRoute in~ ("/", "/login", "/health", "/favicon.ico"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: for each correlated pair, verify the accessed route is genuinely auth-gated and that the client presented no valid session cookie/user context. 2) Contain: if unauthenticated access to protected data is confirmed, treat as active authz bypass — take the app offline or roll back to a good config, upgrade to next-auth@beta, and rotate any secrets/data exposed. 3) Hunt: enumerate every distinct CIp and protected route touched during all error windows, review sensitive-data endpoints (account, admin, API) for actioned requests, and scope which records were reachable while fail-open was active.
let win = 5m;
let AuthErrors = AppServiceHTTPLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
    | where CsUriStem startswith "/api/auth" and ScStatus == 500
    | project ErrTime = TimeGenerated, CsHost, CIp;
AppServiceHTTPLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where ScStatus in (200, 302)
| where not(CsUriStem startswith "/api/auth")
| where not(CsUriStem has_any ("/_next/", ".js", ".css", ".ico", ".png", ".svg", ".woff", ".map"))
| join kind=inner AuthErrors on CsHost, CIp
| where TimeGenerated between (ErrTime .. ErrTime + win)
| project ErrTime, AccessTime = TimeGenerated, CsHost, CIp, CsMethod, ProtectedRoute = CsUriStem, ScStatus
| order by AccessTime desc

CL-STA-1114 (Void Blizzard) Zimbra espionage C2/exfil infrastructure contact AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts any host resolving or connecting to the nine hard-coded C2 domains or nine C2 IPs used by CL-STA-1114 / Void Blizzard to receive stolen Zimbra webmail data (credentials, 2FA scratch codes, CSRF tokens, 90-day mail archive). Article-specific because it matches the exact IOC set Unit 42 attributes to this campaign, not a generic beacon shape. Rationale: Uses the exact nine C2 domains and nine C2 IPs Unit 42 attributes to CL-STA-1114; cross-checked against CISA AA26-204A and The Hacker News which independently confirm the Void Blizzard/LAUNDRY BEAR Zimbra campaign, so the IOCs meet the two-source bar. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa26-204a • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/russian-espionage-group-exploited.html • https://cyberscoop.com/russian-laundry-bear-zimbra-exploit/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel platform or sandbox detonating the same IOCs from a research host
  • Security scanner / EDR retro-hunt actively probing the IOC list
  • DNS sinkhole or protective-DNS appliance logging the resolution before blocking
  • A legitimately-registered look-alike domain reclaimed post-takedown resolving to benign parking infrastructure
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","SenseIR.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the host and the initiating process (browser vs. service); confirm the user has an active Zimbra webmail session and whether the org runs unpatched ZCS (<10.0.18 / <10.1.13). 2) Contain: block all nine domains/IPs at proxy+DNS, isolate the host, and force-reset the affected user's Zimbra password and 2FA scratch codes (the payload steals both). 3) Hunt: pivot on the user/device for the last 90 days of mailbox access, search all endpoints for any of the nine IOCs, and review Zimbra logs for the CSS @import XSS mail that triggered it.

Inbound HTML-attachment lure exploiting Zimbra XSS (CVE-2025-66376) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts inbound emails delivered with an HTML/HTM attachment (or news-headline lure body) to webmail users — the CL-STA-1114 delivery vector that carries the obfuscated Base64/SVG payload abusing Zimbra's CSS @import XSS. Article-specific in that it targets the zero-click HTML-borne exploit rather than generic malicious attachments. Rationale: Article states initial access is a phishing email with an HTML attachment or embedded HTML carrying the Base64/SVG payload; corroborating CISA/SentinelOne detail confirms CVE-2025-66376 fires on viewing crafted HTML mail, so inbound HTML attachments to webmail users are the delivery pivot. Kept as hunting given benign HTML attachments are common. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2025-66376/ • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa26-204a
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1203
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Marketing/newsletter platforms that send rich HTML as an attachment
  • Automated report/invoice systems delivering .htm exports
  • Internal ticketing or monitoring tools emailing HTML dashboards inbound via a relay
  • Recruiter/CV emails with HTML resumes
Suppression filter
| where SenderFromDomain !in~ ("news.example-vendor.com") and not (SenderMailFromDomain endswith "mailchimpapp.net")
Response runbook
1) Triage: open the HTML attachment in a sandbox and grep for CSS @import, invisible <svg onload>, atob()/Base64 blobs, or references to the nine campaign domains. 2) Contain: if malicious, purge the message tenant-wide (soft-delete), block sender + any embedded domain, and reset the recipient's Zimbra credentials and 2FA scratch codes. 3) Hunt: confirm whether the org runs unpatched ZCS, and correlate the recipient against the C2-contact detection to see if exfiltration already occurred.
EmailAttachmentInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileType in~ ("html","htm")
| join kind=inner (
    EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
    | where DeliveryAction in ("Delivered","DeliveredAsSpam")
  ) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, SenderMailFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, FileName, FileType, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation, ThreatTypes
| order by Timestamp desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
EmailAttachmentInfo
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where FileType in~ ("html","htm")
| join kind=inner (
    EmailEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
    | where DeliveryAction in ("Delivered","DeliveredAsSpam")
  ) on NetworkMessageId
| project TimeGenerated, SenderFromAddress, SenderMailFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, FileName, FileType, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation, ThreatTypes
| order by TimeGenerated desc
Browser-initiated webmail data exfiltration to CL-STA-1114 C2 AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts a browser process (the authenticated Zimbra session) making outbound HTTP connections to the campaign's C2 domains/IPs — the moment the injected JavaScript ships stolen credentials, 2FA scratch codes, CSRF tokens and mail archive off-box. Distinct from the broad C2 detection by requiring a browser initiator and HTTP egress shape. Rationale: Combines the campaign's confirmed C2 IOC set with a browser-process initiator, because the CVE-2025-66376 XSS runs inside the authenticated Zimbra browser session and the injected JS exfiltrates over HTTP — a browser hitting these specific hosts is high-fidelity exfil, not generic web traffic. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa26-204a • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/russian-espionage-group-exploited.html
ATT&CKT1041 T1539 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Analyst manually browsing to a seized/sinkholed C2 domain during investigation
  • Browser prefetch/DNS-preconnect to a domain reclaimed post-takedown
  • URL-reputation browser extension pinging a look-alike domain
  • Sandbox/detonation VM using a real browser to detonate the sample
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--headless" and DeviceName !in~ ("SANDBOX-DETONATE01")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the browser had an active Zimbra session and inspect the request (POST body size, user-agent) for outbound credential/mail data. 2) Contain: isolate the host, block the C2 at proxy+DNS, and immediately reset the user's Zimbra password, 2FA scratch codes, and invalidate active sessions/CSRF tokens. 3) Hunt: sweep all browsers org-wide for the nine IOCs, review the mailbox for 90-day access anomalies, and check whether the org's ZCS is unpatched.

Unpatched Zimbra Collaboration exposed to CVE-2025-66376 (Void Blizzard target) AIExploitation High
Surfaces endpoints/servers running Zimbra Collaboration versions vulnerable to CVE-2025-66376 — the CSS @import stored-XSS that CL-STA-1114 exploits zero-click. Directly supports the article's proactive-patching guidance by listing exploitable ZCS instances (10.0<10.0.18, 10.1<10.1.13). Rationale: Uses the concrete CVE-2025-66376 identifier confirmed by SentinelOne's vuln database and the CISA advisory (affected 10.0<10.0.18 / 10.1<10.1.13); a TVM exposure hunt is the cleanest way to operationalize the article's patch-now message. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2025-66376/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/russian-hackers-exploit-zimbra-zero-click-flaw-for-email-theft/
ATT&CKT1203 T1190
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • ZCS host already patched to 10.0.18/10.1.13 but TVM inventory lagging a scan cycle
  • Non-production/staging Zimbra instance not internet-exposed
  • Defender TVM mis-parsing a Zimbra build string on a Linux appliance
  • Decommissioned server still present in the device inventory
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the Zimbra build and whether the Classic Web Client (the vulnerable UI) is enabled and internet-reachable. 2) Contain: schedule emergency patch to 10.0.18 / 10.1.13, or disable the Classic UI / apply the vendor mitigation in the interim. 3) Hunt: on each exposed host, correlate against the C2-contact and browser-exfil detections and review Zimbra mail logs for crafted HTML messages abusing CSS @import.

C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
